title: Hindi to Marathi Greetings & First Sentences
description: Bridge your Hindi into Marathi greetings and first sentences: नमस्ते→नमस्कार, मेरा नाम→माझं नाव, मुझे चाहिए→मला पाहिजे — mapping by mapping.
h1: Hindi → Marathi: Greetings & Your First Sentences
intro: If you know Hindi, your first Marathi sentences are closer than you think — but not identical. This page maps the greeting-and-introduction bridge row by row: what carries over, what shifts sound, and what changes shape entirely.
Each row shows the Hindi you know, the Marathi that matches, the English meaning, and the one grammar note that matters for that pair. These are Unit 01 bridge lessons from the Bol Marathi course.
tip: Read each pair aloud, Hindi then Marathi — your ear already knows how close they are.

sections.heading: What carries over directly
paragraphs: नमस्ते → नमस्कार, and it works any time of day. Sentence skeletons carry over too: both languages put the verb last, so the shape of आप कैसे हैं? and तू कसा आहेस? is the same shape.

sections.heading: Where Hindi and Marathi part ways
paragraphs: Three splits to know on day one: possession (मेरा नाम → माझं नाव — Marathi नाव is neuter), need (मुझे चाहिए → मला पाहिजे — one fused expression), and the continuous tense (खा रहा हूँ → खातो आहे — verb + तो + आहे instead of रहा/रही).
None of these require new grammar concepts; they are Hindi logic wearing Marathi endings — which is exactly what the bridge rows below drill.

mistakes.why: नाव is neuter in Marathi, so the possessive is माझं, not माझा (and not Hindi मेरा).
Marathi continuous = verb + तो + आहे. रहा never appears.
चाहिए has no Marathi life; the fused form is मला … पाहिजे.

mcq.question: “मुझे चाहिए” in Marathi is…
mcq.explanation: मला पाहिजे — the fused need-expression from Unit 01.

mcq.question: “How are you?” (to a male friend) in Marathi?
mcq.explanation: कसा agrees with the person addressed: masculine कसा, feminine कशी.

faq.question: How do you say hello in Marathi if you know Hindi?
faq.answer: नमस्ते becomes नमस्कार — and it works at any hour. Add शुभ सकाळ (good morning) and शुभ रात्री (good night) for time-specific greetings.

faq.question: Is Marathi grammar the same as Hindi?
faq.answer: The frame is the same (subject–object–verb, postpositions, gender agreement), but Marathi adds a neuter gender, fuses expressions like मला पाहिजे, and forms the continuous tense with verb + तो + आहे.

title: Hindi to Marathi Daily Conversation: Survival Sentences
description: Everyday survival sentences mapped Hindi to Marathi — तैयार→तयार, मदद→मदत, चाहिए→पाहिजे, नहीं चाहिए→नको — with the grammar behind each pair.
intro: Six survival-sentence mappings from Unit 02 of the Bol Marathi course: being ready, asking for help, saying what is yours, question words, polite imperatives, and the need/don't-want pair. Each row shows the Hindi, the Marathi, the English, and one grammar note.
The theme of this page is sound shift plus fusion: मदद → मदत and तैयार → तयार are the same words wearing Marathi endings, while नहीं चाहिए fuses into the single word नको.
tip: मदत before मदद: help is the one word you never want to mispronounce.

sections.heading: Sound shifts you can bank on
paragraphs: A reliable early pattern: several Hindi words ending in a consonant + अ pick up a त in Marathi — मदद → मदत. Others drop the tail vowel: तैयार stays तैयार. When in doubt, check the table; the shifts are regular enough to become instinct within a week.

sections.heading: The fused forms
paragraphs: Marathi likes single words where Hindi uses phrases: चाहिए → पाहिजे, नहीं चाहिए → नको. Learn the pair पाहिजे/नको as one unit; Unit 02's sentence मला चहा नको, पाणी द्या shows both halves of the conversation.

mistakes.why: Same word, Marathi ending: the final द becomes त.
Marathi fuses the whole idea into one word — the highest-utility negation you will learn.

mcq.question: “Help” in Marathi?
mcq.explanation: मदत (madat) — Hindi मदद with the Marathi त ending.

mcq.question: “Ready” in Marathi?
mcq.explanation: तयार — same spelling, no tail vowel change here.

translate.note: From Unit 02 — both halves shift: मदद→मदत and चाहिए→पाहिजे.

faq.question: What are the first differences a Hindi speaker hits in Marathi?
faq.answer: Fused expressions (पाहिजे, नको), sound shifts (मदद→मदत), the neuter gender, and the continuous tense built with तो + आहे instead of रहा.

faq.question: How do you ask for help in Marathi?
faq.answer: मला मदत पाहिजे (I need help). In an emergency the single word मदत! works.

title: Hindi to Marathi Question Words: क्या → काय
description: All six question words mapped Hindi to Marathi — क्या→काय, कहाँ→कुठे, कब→कधी, कैसे→कसे, कौन→कोण, क्यों→का — with example questions.
h1: Hindi → Marathi: Question Words (काय, कुठे, कधी)
intro: Six pairs, one pattern: Hindi question words starting with क map to Marathi question words starting with क. क्या→काय, कहाँ→कुठे, कब→कधी, कैसे→कसे, कौन→कोण, क्यों→का. Unit 07 of the course is built entirely on these six.
The best news on this page: question words stay in place. कुठे जात आहेस? puts कुठे exactly where कहाँ sits in कहाँ जा रहे हो? There is no word-order tax on questions.
tip: Learn the six as a क-family: काय कुठे कधी कसे कोण का — one breath, all six.

sections.heading: The क-family
paragraphs: Both languages front-load interrogatives with क, which makes the mapping feel designed. The two that need attention: क्यों becomes single-syllable का, and कौन becomes कोण — the vowel changes, the role doesn't.

sections.heading: Question words in action
paragraphs: Unit 07's lesson sentences show the full swap: कुठे जात आहेस? पुणे. (Where are you going? Pune.) and कधी येत आहेस? उद्या. (When are you coming? Tomorrow.) Notice आहेस tagging along at the end — the verb stays last, as always.

mistakes.wrong: Translating क्यों as a long word
mistakes.why: उदाहरण: का आलात? (Why did you come?) — short and final-position-friendly.
The vowel is ओ, and the final ण is retroflex — कोण, not कुन or कौन.

mcq.question: “Where” in Marathi?
mcq.explanation: कुठे (kuṭhe) = where; कधी is when.

mcq.question: काय आहे? means…
mcq.explanation: काय = what — the opener of Unit 07.

mcq.question: “Why” in Marathi?
mcq.explanation: का (kā) = why — a single syllable.

fill.hint: Answer is a place, so the question word is…

faq.question: What are the six Marathi question words?
faq.answer: काय (what), कुठे (where), कधी (when), कसे (how), कोण (who), का (why) — each mapping to its Hindi क-counterpart.

faq.question: Do Marathi questions change word order?
faq.answer: No — the question word stays where the answer would go, and the verb stays last: तू कुठे जात आहेस?

title: Hindi to Marathi Travel Words: Trains, Tickets & Stays
description: 12 Hindi-to-Marathi travel mappings — transport, booking, stations, hotels and directions — with the vocabulary travellers actually need in Maharashtra.
intro: Twelve bridge rows from Units 14–15 covering a full journey: landscapes and directions, transport modes, booking and platforms, hotels and local transport. Each maps the Hindi phrase you know to the Marathi you will hear at a Maharashtra station or ticket counter.

Much travel vocabulary is shared — बस, टिकीट, हॉटेल — and the cardinal directions are identical: उत्तर, दक्षिण, पूर्व, पश्चिम. What changes are the transport words themselves and the spelling conventions around loanwords.
tip: Before a trip, memorize the booking row (बुक करा, कन्फर्म, वेटिंग) and platform sentence first — timetables forgive, queues don't.

sections.heading: The good news: directions and half the nouns
paragraphs: उत्तर दक्षिण पूर्व पश्चिम are letter-for-letter Hindi. नदी, पठार, वेटिंग, टर्मिनल, गेट, लॉज cross over untouched. You already own half the travel page.

sections.heading: What actually changes
paragraphs: Train is रेल्वे in Marathi (though ट्रेन is universally understood, and course sentences use both). झील becomes सरोवर, पेड़ becomes झाड, जानवर becomes प्राणी. And watch the loanword spellings: Marathi writes प्लॅटफॉर्म, हॉटेल and शेअरिंग with its own conventions (ॅ and ऑ).

mistakes.why: Marathi and Hindi spell English loanwords differently — signs in Maharashtra use the ॅ convention.
झील is understood by bilinguals but सरोवर is the Marathi word on maps and in speech.

mcq.question: “Train” in formal Marathi?
mcq.explanation: रेल्वे is the Marathi word; ट्रेन is understood everywhere, and विमान is a flight.

mcq.question: Which set is identical in Hindi and Marathi?
mcq.explanation: उत्तर दक्षिण पूर्व पश्चिम — the directions never change.

translate.note: From Unit 15 — note मुंबईला (to Mumbai) and the relative clause जाणारा.

faq.question: How different is travel Marathi from Hindi?
faq.answer: Directions, bookings and stays are mostly shared; transport names and nature words shift (ट्रेन→रेल्वे, झील→सरोवर, जानवर→प्राणी), and loanwords take Marathi spellings with ॅ and ऑ.

faq.question: How do you ask “which platform” in Marathi?
faq.answer: प्लॅटफॉर्म नंबर कोणता? — or state it: प्लॅटफॉर्म नंबर पाच आहे. The word order matches the Hindi you already know.

title: Hindi to Marathi Family & Home: Relations, Rooms, Daily Life
description: Family relations and home vocabulary mapped Hindi to Marathi — relations, rooms, everyday household words — from Units 03, 05, 20.
intro: Family and home vocabulary from Units 03, 05, 20 mapped Hindi to Marathi — relations (चाचा→काका, चाची→काकी), rooms (कमरा→खोली), everyday objects. Each row shows the Hindi you know, the Marathi that matches, and the one grammar note that matters.
Marathi keeps gender in relations explicitly: काका/काकी (uncle/aunt), मामा/मामी, दादा/दादी, मामू/मामी — the feminine form is always there. Hindi merges some; Marathi separates.
tip: Learn relations in pairs: काका/काकी, मामा/मामी, दादा/दादी — the feminine form is the same root + ई.

sections.heading: Relations — gender is explicit
paragraphs: Hindi चाचा/चाची maps cleanly to काका/काकी. But दादा is both grandfather and elder brother — context tells you. भाऊ/बहिण are the sibling words; कोई/कोणी for someone/anyone.

sections.heading: Rooms and fixtures
paragraphs: कमरा → खोली, दरवाजा → दार, खिड़की → खिडकी, आईना → आरसा, चाबी → चावी. The Hindi speaker's आरसा moment: mirror is not आईना in Marathi.

mistakes.why: आईना is Hindi; आरसा is the Marathi word — no sound overlap, must learn fresh.

mistakes.right: भाऊ = elder brother; दादा = grandfather or elder brother (context)
mistakes.why: Marathi distinguishes: भाऊ is the sibling word, दादा is grandfather (and respectfully, elder brother).
Systematic Hindi ब → Marathi व shift in loans: चाबी→चावी, सब्जी→भाजी spirit.

mcq.question: Elder brother in Marathi?
mcq.explanation: भाऊ = elder brother; दादा = grandfather.

mcq.question: Mirror in Marathi?
mcq.explanation: आरसा (ārsā) — the clearest Hindi→Marathi swap on this page.

mcq.question: Room in Marathi?
mcq.explanation: खोली (khoḷī) = room; घर = house.

faq.question: How do you say “uncle/aunt” in Marathi?
faq.answer: काका/काकी (father's brother/wife), मामा/मामी (mother's brother/wife) — gender is explicit in every pair.

faq.question: What is the Marathi word for “mirror”?
faq.answer: आरसा — not आईना. This is one of the few household words with zero sound overlap.

title: Hindi to Marathi Sentence Patterns: SOV, Particles, Tense
description: Core sentence patterns mapped Hindi to Marathi — SOV order, particles (ने, को, से), continuous tense (रहा→तो+आहे), possession — from Units 04, 05.
intro: Sentence-level mappings from Units 04–05: both languages are SOV, but Marathi adds a neuter gender, fuses postpositions (मुझे→मला, को→कडून), and builds continuous tense with verb+तो+आहे instead of रहा/रही. Each row maps the Hindi pattern to the Marathi pattern with the grammar note.
The good news: word order is the same. The work is in the particles and the fused forms.
tip: Continuous tense = verb root + तो + आहे (खातो आहे, जात आहे, बोलतो आहे). Drop रहा/रही entirely.

sections.heading: Postposition fusion
paragraphs: Hindi मुझे → Marathi मला, को → कडून, से → कडून, के लिए → साठी. These are single fused forms where Hindi uses a separate postposition. Memorize the fused pairs; they appear in every sentence.

sections.heading: The continuous tense rewrite
paragraphs: Hindi खा रहा हूँ → Marathi मी खातो आहे. The pattern: verb root + तो + आहे (masculine), ती + आहे (feminine), ते + आहे (neuter). No रहा/रही anywhere.

mistakes.why: Marathi continuous = verb root + तो + आहे. रहा never appears.
पसंद है has no Marathi life; the fused form is मला … आवडते.
Three genders, three forms — the noun decides.

mcq.question: “I am eating” in Marathi?
mcq.explanation: Verb root खा + तो + आहे = खातो आहे.

mcq.question: “To me” (dative) in Marathi?
mcq.explanation: मला — the fused dative form, replaces Hindi मुझे.

mcq.question: Continuous tense marker in Marathi?
mcq.explanation: तो + आहे (masc), ती + आहे (fem), ते + आहे (neut).

translate.note: Verb root जा + तो + आहे = जात आहे.

faq.question: Is Marathi word order the same as Hindi?
faq.answer: Yes — both are SOV. The differences are in particles (fused forms), gender (neuter added), and continuous tense (तो+आहे).

faq.question: How do you form the continuous tense in Marathi?
faq.answer: Verb root + तो + आहे (masc), ती + आहे (fem), ते + आहे (neut). Example: खातो आहे, पडते आहे, बोलतो आहे.

title: Hindi to Marathi Pronouns & People Words: I, You, We, They
description: Pronouns and people words mapped Hindi to Marathi — मैं→मी, तू→तू, आप→तुम्ही/आप, वह→तो/ती/ते — with gender, honorifics and case forms from Unit 05.
intro: Pronouns and people words from Unit 05 mapped Hindi to Marathi: personal pronouns (मैं→मी, तू→तू, आप→तुम्ही/आप, वह→तो/ती/ते), demonstratives (यह→हा/ही/हे, वह→तो/ती/ते), question pronouns (कौन→कोण, क्या→काय). Each row shows the Hindi, the Marathi, and the gender/case note.
Marathi adds a neuter gender (ते/हे) and splits the honorific आप into तुम्ही (plural respectful) and आप (formal singular). The demonstratives mirror the pronoun genders exactly.
tip: Demonstratives = pronoun genders made visible: हा/ही/हे = तो/ती/ते near the speaker. Learn one set, you know both.

sections.heading: Personal pronouns — three genders, two honorifics
paragraphs: मी (I), तू (you informal), तुम्ही (you respectful plural/older), आप (formal singular — rare in speech). Third person: तो (he), ती (she), ते (it/they neuter). The neuter ते is the new piece for Hindi speakers.

sections.heading: Demonstratives mirror pronouns
paragraphs: हा/ही/हे (this) matches तो/ती/ते (that) in gender exactly. इथे/तिथे (here/there) and असा/तसा (like this/like that) follow the same near/far split.

mistakes.why: तू is intimate/informal only. Hindi speakers often overuse तू because आप covers both in Hindi.

mistakes.wrong: Assuming वह maps to one word
mistakes.right: वह → तो (he) / ती (she) / ते (it) — gender is mandatory
mistakes.why: Marathi has no gender-neutral third-person singular.

mistakes.right: इथे = here; येथे is a variant, standard is इथे
mistakes.why: Course standard is इथे/तिथे.

mcq.question: “He” in Marathi?
mcq.explanation: तो = he (masculine).

mcq.question: Formal “you” in Marathi?
mcq.explanation: तुम्ही = respectful you. आप exists but is rare in speech.

mcq.question: Neuter “it/this”?
mcq.explanation: हे (he) = neuter this/it.

faq.question: How many genders does Marathi have?
faq.answer: Three — masculine, feminine, neuter. Hindi has two; the neuter (ते/हे/माझे) is the new one to learn.

faq.question: What is the formal “you” in Marathi?
faq.answer: तुम्ही (respectful plural/older). The Hindi आप splits into तुम्ही (common) and आप (very formal, rare).

title: Hindi to Marathi Shopping: Market, Prices, Bargaining
description: Shopping vocabulary mapped Hindi to Marathi — prices, quantities, bargaining, payment — from Unit 09.
intro: Shopping and market vocabulary from Unit 09 mapped Hindi to Marathi — quantities (किलो, पाव, आधा), prices (कितना→किती, महँगा→महाग), bargaining (कम करो→कमी करा), payment (नकद→रोख, ऑनलाइन→ऑनलाइन). Each row maps the Hindi phrase to the Marathi sentence with the grammar note.
The quantities and bargaining lines are identical in structure — एक किलो, आधा किलो, थोडं कमी करा — making this one of the fastest pages for Hindi speakers to internalize.
tip: थोडं कमी करा, कृपया — the single most useful bargaining line. Say it with a smile; vendors expect it.

sections.heading: Quantities — identical structure
paragraphs: एक किलो, आधा किलो, पाव किलो, दोन किलो — the Hindi speaker already knows these. The Marathi noun follows exactly as in Hindi: एक किलो भाजी, आधा किलो टोमॅटो.

sections.heading: Bargaining lines
paragraphs: किती आहे? (How much?), थोडं कमी करा (reduce a little), हे छान आहे (this is good), मी घेईन (I'll take it), बिल द्या (give the bill). The grammar is the same; only the vocabulary shifts.

mistakes.why: Hindi कितना/कितनी/कितने; Marathi collapses to किती for all.
Same root, Marathi drops the nasal: महँगा → महाग.
नकद is understood but रोख is the everyday Marathi word.

mcq.question: How much? in Marathi
mcq.explanation: किती — single form for all genders/numbers.

mcq.question: “Reduce a little” in Marathi?
mcq.explanation: थोडं कमी करा — exact Unit 09 line.

mcq.question: Cash in Marathi?
mcq.explanation: रोख (rokh) — everyday word; नकद is formal.

faq.question: How do you bargain in Marathi?
faq.answer: थोडं कमी करा, कृपया — reduce a little, please. The polite कृपया makes it standard etiquette.

faq.question: What is the Marathi word for “expensive”?
faq.answer: महाग (mahāg) — same root as महँगा, nasal dropped.

title: Hindi to Marathi Health & Body: Symptoms, Doctor Visit
description: Health and body vocabulary mapped Hindi to Marathi — body parts, symptoms, doctor sentences — from Units 10, 17.
intro: Health and body vocabulary from Units 10 and 17 mapped Hindi to Marathi — body parts (सिर→डोकं, पेट→पोट, हाथ→हात), symptoms (दर्द→दुखते, बुखार→ताप, खाँसी→खोकला), doctor sentences (डॉक्टर, मुझे चाहिए→मला पाहिजे). Each row shows the Hindi, the Marathi, and the grammar note.
The pattern माझे … दुखते (my … hurts) with body part as subject mirrors Hindi मेरा … दुख रहा है — the subject-verb agreement carries over. The shift is in the body part words themselves.
tip: Body part as subject: माझं डोके दुखते (my head hurts). The body part is the grammatical subject — same logic as Hindi.

sections.heading: Body parts — the shifts
paragraphs: सिर → डोकं, पेट → पोट, हाथ → हात, पैर → पाय, आँख → डोळा, कान → कान (same), नाक → नाक (same), दाँत → दात. The unchanged ones (कान, नाक) are free; the shifted ones (डोकं, पोट, डोळा, दात) are the ones to drill.

sections.heading: Symptoms — the pattern carries
paragraphs: दुखते (hurts) with body part subject: माझं डोके दुखते, माझे पोट दुखते. ताप (fever), खोकला (cough), उलटी (vomiting), दस्त (diarrhea) — all take मला pattern: मला ताप आहे, मला खोकला आहे.

mistakes.why: Symptoms take the dative मला pattern: मला ताप आहे, मला खोकला आहे.
आँख is Hindi; डोळा is the Marathi word — no sound overlap.

mistakes.wrong: मेरा पेट दुख रहा है word-for-word
mistakes.why: Body part as subject works, but the possessive and body word shift: मेरा→माझे, पेट→पोट, दुख रहा है→दुखते.

mcq.question: Headache in Marathi?
mcq.explanation: माझं डोके दुखते — body part as subject, neuter agreement.

mcq.question: Fever in Marathi?
mcq.explanation: ताप (tāp) — everyday word; बुखार is understood but ताप is standard.

mcq.question: Stomach in Marathi?
mcq.explanation: पोट (poṭ) — stomach.

faq.question: How do you say “my stomach hurts” in Marathi?
faq.answer: माझे पोट दुखते — body part as subject, neuter possessive माझे, verb दुखते.

faq.question: What is the Marathi word for “cough”?
faq.answer: खोकला (khoklā) — मला खोकला आहे (I have a cough).

title: Hindi to Marathi Time & Seasons: Clock, Calendar, Weather
description: Time, seasons and calendar mapped Hindi to Marathi — clock words, day parts, seasons, dates — from Units 16, 14.
intro: Time, seasons and calendar words from Units 14 and 16 mapped Hindi to Marathi — clock (घंटा→तास, मिनट→मिनिट, बजे→वाजले), day parts (सुबह→सकाळ, दोपहर→दुपार, शाम→संध्याकाळ, रात→रात्र), seasons (गर्मी→उन्हाळा, बरसात→पावसाळा, सर्दी→हिवाळा, बसंत→वसंत). Each row shows the Hindi, the Marathi, and the one trap to avoid.
The big trap for Hindi speakers: काल means YESTERDAY in Marathi (tomorrow is उद्या). This is the single most dangerous false friend on the calendar.
tip: काल = yesterday (not tomorrow). उद्या = tomorrow. Write it on a sticky note until it sticks.

sections.heading: The काल trap
paragraphs: Hindi कल = tomorrow OR yesterday (context). Marathi splits it: उद्या = tomorrow, काल = yesterday. This is the #1 calendar mistake for Hindi speakers — drill it until automatic.

sections.heading: Clock words
paragraphs: घंटा → तास, मिनट → मिनिट, बजे → वाजले (the verb, not a noun). साडे पाच वाजले = half past five. The half-hour marker साडे is the only new grammar piece; the numbers are shared.

mistakes.why: The most dangerous false friend in the time system. Hindi कल does both; Marathi separates them.
Marathi uses वाजले (struck) as the verb: पाच वाजले = 5 o'clock struck.
गर्मी = heat (noun); उन्हाळा = the summer season. Same split as Hindi but the word is different.

mcq.question: Tomorrow in Marathi?
mcq.explanation: उद्या = tomorrow. काल = yesterday.

mcq.question: Half past five in Marathi?
mcq.explanation: साडे पाच वाजले — साडे = half, वाजले = struck.

mcq.question: Monsoon in Marathi?
mcq.explanation: पावसाळा (pāvasāḷā) — the monsoon season.

fill.sentence: आता ___ वाजले. (It is now half past five.)

faq.question: What is the biggest time trap for Hindi speakers?
faq.answer: काल means yesterday in Marathi, not tomorrow. Tomorrow is उद्या. This is the #1 mistake.

faq.question: How do you say “5 o'clock” in Marathi?
faq.answer: पाच वाजले — the verb वाजले (struck) replaces Hindi बजे.

title: Hindi to Marathi Emotions: Feelings, Moods, Inner States
description: Emotions and inner states mapped Hindi to Marathi — आनंद, राग, भीती, काळजी, भूक, तहान — with the मला…आहे pattern from Unit 17.
intro: Emotions and inner states from Unit 17 mapped Hindi to Marathi — आनंद (happiness), राग (anger), भीती (fear), काळजी (worry), लाज (shame), गौरव (pride), and the body-states भूक (hunger), तहान (thirst), झोप (sleepiness). Each row shows the Hindi, the Marathi, and the मला…आहे pattern note.

The grammar key: feelings and body-states arrive TO you in Marathi — मला आनंद आहे (I have happiness → I am happy), मला भूक लागली आहे (hunger has hit me). Hindi मुझे … है works the same way; the words shift.
tip: Learn in opposite pairs: आनंद/दुःख, भीती/धैर्य, काळजी/निश्चिंती, भूक/तृप्ती — pairs stick better than lists.

sections.heading: The मला…आहे pattern
paragraphs: Feelings are things that happen TO you: मला राग आला (anger came to me), मला भीती वाटते (fear feels to me), मला भूक लागली आहे (hunger has struck me). The Hindi मुझे … है maps directly — just swap the vocabulary.

sections.heading: The राग trap
paragraphs: Hindi राग = musical mode. Marathi राग = anger. Same spelling, opposite vibe. This is the highest-frequency false friend on this page — flag it mentally.

mistakes.why: Hindi राग (melody) ≠ Marathi राग (anger). The word is identical; the meaning is not.

mistakes.wrong: मी आनंद आहे for “I am happy”
mistakes.why: Happiness arrives TO you: मला (to me) + आनंद (happiness) + आहे (is).
Standard Marathi keeps the ः; writing दुख is the Hindi spelling habit.

mcq.question: Anger in Marathi?
mcq.explanation: राग (rāg) = anger — not music, as in Hindi.

mcq.question: “I am afraid” in Marathi?
mcq.explanation: मला भीती वाटते — fear feels to me (dative + verb वाटणे).

mcq.question: Hunger in Marathi?
mcq.explanation: भूक (bhūk) — the dative pattern: मला भूक लागली आहे.

translate.note: Unit 17 — आनंदी (happy) is the adjective form of आनंद.

faq.question: How do you say “I am sad” in Marathi?
faq.answer: मला दुःख आहे or मी दुःखी आहे — the curriculum sentence is मला थोडं दुःख आहे (I feel a little sad).

faq.question: Is राग the same in Hindi and Marathi?
faq.answer: No — Hindi राग = musical mode; Marathi राग = anger. This is the top false friend on this page.

title: Hindi to Marathi Work & Career: Jobs, Office, Professions
description: Work and career vocabulary mapped Hindi to Marathi — jobs, office, traditional professions, modern roles — from Units 11, 19, 23.
intro: Work and career vocabulary from Units 11, 19, 23 mapped Hindi to Marathi — modern roles (इंजीनियर→अभियंता, वकील→वकील, डॉक्टर→डॉक्टर), traditional professions (बढ़ई→सुतार, लोहार→लोहार, सुनार→सोनार, दर्जी→शिंपी), office words (नौकरी→नोकरी, वेतन→पगार, मीटिंग→बैठक, छुट्टी→सुट्टी). Each row maps the Hindi to the Marathi with the grammar note.
Many traditional professions are also surnames in Maharashtra — सुतार, लोहार, सोनार, शिंपी, न्हावी, धोबी, माळी, गवळी. Knowing the word means you recognize the surname too.
tip: Traditional professions = surnames: सुतार, लोहार, सोनार, शिंपी, न्हावी, धोबी, माळी, गवळी. The vocabulary and the family name are identical.

sections.heading: Traditional professions — surnames you will meet
paragraphs: सुतार (carpenter), लोहार (blacksmith), सोनार (goldsmith), शिंपी (tailor), न्हावी (barber), धोबी (washerman), माळी (gardener), गवळी (milkman) — identical words serve as job titles and family names across Maharashtra.

sections.heading: Modern office
paragraphs: नोकरी (job), पगार (salary), बैठक (meeting), सुट्टी (leave), संगणक (computer), बिल (bill), प्रमोशन (promotion), प्रोजेक्ट (project) — the words for your first day, your payslip, your career growth.

mistakes.why: Hindi सिपाही = soldier; Marathi शिपाई is the office attendant. The soldier is सैनिक — direct false friend.
मला काम आहे (I have work to do) vs माझी नोकरी आहे (I have a job). Hindi काम/नौकरी follows the same split.

mistakes.right: मालक/अधिकारी — बॉस is understood but मालक is the Marathi word
mistakes.why: Loanwords work but the native terms carry more respect in formal contexts.

mcq.question: Salary in Marathi?
mcq.explanation: पगार (pagār) — everyday word; वेतन is formal.

mcq.question: A tailor in Marathi?
mcq.explanation: शिंपी (śimpī) = tailor; the surname Shimpī comes from this.

mcq.question: Leave/holiday in Marathi?
mcq.explanation: सुट्टी (suṭṭī) — the everyday word.

fill.hint: Unit 19 office sentence — loanword used as-is.

faq.question: What is the Marathi word for “salary”?
faq.answer: पगार (pagār) — everyday; वेतन is formal/official.

faq.question: Are traditional professions also surnames?
faq.answer: Yes — सुतार, लोहार, सोनार, शिंपी, न्हावी, धोबी, माळी, गवळी are both job titles and common surnames in Maharashtra.

title: Hindi to Marathi Review: Grammar & Vocab Recap
description: Review of essential Hindi-to-Marathi bridges — fused forms, sound shifts, gender, continuous tense, question words — from Units 01–20.
intro: A review bridge pulling the highest-leverage patterns from Units 01–20: fused forms (पाहिजे, नको, मला), sound shifts (मदद→मदत, तयार, चावी), three genders (माझा/माझी/माझे), continuous tense (तो+आहे), question words (काय, कुठे, कधी, कसे, कोण, का), and the dative pattern for feelings/symptoms (मला…आहे). Each row is a Hindi→Marathi mapping with the one note that makes it stick.
This page is the pre-trip or pre-exam checklist — if these 20 rows are automatic, the rest of the course builds on solid ground.
tip: If you know these 20 rows cold, you have the skeleton of Marathi. Everything else is vocabulary hanging on this frame.

sections.heading: The 5 fused forms to never forget
paragraphs: 1) चाहिए → पाहिजे  2) नहीं चाहिए → नको  3) मुझे → मला  4) को/से/के लिए → कडून/साठी  5) यह/वह → हा/ही/हे, तो/ती/ते. These appear in every conversation.

sections.heading: The 3 sound shifts that cover 80%
paragraphs: 1) Hindi द/द → Marathi त/त (मदद→मदत, चाबी→चावी, सब्जी→भाजी spirit). 2) Hindi nasal drop (महँगा→महाग, गंगा→गंगा same). 3) Hindi आ → Marathi अ/अ (तयार, आरसा).

mistakes.why: Fused forms are mandatory, not optional — they are the grammar.

mistakes.right: Neuter is real: ते, हे, माझे, सोपे, खाते आहे
mistakes.why: Hindi has two genders; Marathi has three. Ignoring neuter breaks agreement everywhere.
The marker is the verb root + तो/ती/ते + आहे. रहा has no place in Marathi.

mcq.question: “I need” in Marathi?
mcq.explanation: मला पाहिजे — the fused need form.

mcq.question: Continuous “he is going”?
mcq.explanation: तो जात आहे — root जा + तो + आहे.

mcq.question: Neuter “this book”?
mcq.explanation: पुस्तक is neuter → हे पुस्तक.

translate.note: Fused need + dative — the pattern from Unit 01.

faq.question: What are the top 5 Hindi→Marathi patterns to master first?
faq.answer: 1) पाहिजे/नको (need/don't want)  2) मला (to me)  3) कडून/साठी (from/for)  4) तो+आहे (continuous)  5) हा/ही/हे (gendered this).

faq.question: Do I need to learn all three genders?
faq.answer: Yes — neuter is not optional. Words like पाणी (water), पुस्तक (book), घर (house), खाते (eating) are neuter and appear constantly.

title: Hindi to Marathi Advanced: Passive, Causative
description: Advanced structures mapped Hindi to Marathi — passive, causative, relative-correlative, conditionals — from Unit 21.
intro: Advanced structures from Unit 21 mapped Hindi to Marathi — passive voice (किया जाता है → केला जाते), causative (करवाता है → करवते), relative-correlative pairs (जो…वह → जो…तो), complex conditionals (अगर…तो → जर…तर). Each row shows the Hindi structure, the Marathi equivalent, and the grammar shift.
Marathi passive uses the verb root + याचे/याचे + जाते (केला जाते, खाल्ले जाते). Causative adds व/वव (खववते = makes eat, बोलवते = makes speak). The relative-correlative pair is जो…तो (not जो…वह).
tip: Passive = root + याचे + जाते. Causative = root + व/वव. Relative = जो…तो. Three patterns, infinite sentences.

sections.heading: Passive — the याचे+जाते frame
paragraphs: Hindi किया जाता है → Marathi केला जाते. The pattern: past participle (केला, खाल्ले, केले) + याचे + जाते. The agent (by whom) uses कडून: मी कडून केला जाते (done by me).

sections.heading: Causative — the व/वव marker
paragraphs: Hindi करवाता है → Marathi करवते. खववते (makes eat), बोलवते (makes speak), लिहवते (makes write). The causative marker व/वव attaches to the verb root before the tense ending.

mistakes.wrong: Using किया जाता है structure directly
mistakes.right: केला जाते — past participle + याचे + जाते
mistakes.why: Marathi passive is not a word-for-word translation of Hindi passive; the morphology is different.

mistakes.right: जो…तो — the correlative is तो, not वह
mistakes.why: Marathi's relative-correlative pair is जो…तो. वह never appears as the correlate.

mistakes.right: Check if the verb is already causative (बोलवणे = to make speak); double causative is ungrammatical
mistakes.why: Some verbs are inherently causative; adding another व creates nonsense.

mcq.question: Passive of “to do” in Marathi?
mcq.explanation: केला जाते — past participle केला + याचे + जाते.

mcq.question: Causative of “to eat” (खाणे)?
mcq.explanation: खववते — root खा + वव + ते = makes eat.

mcq.question: Relative-correlative pair in Marathi?
mcq.explanation: जो…तो — जो introduces, तो correlates.

faq.question: How do you form the passive in Marathi?
faq.answer: Past participle + याचे + जाते — e.g., केला जाते (is done), खाल्ले जाते (is eaten), लिखले जाते (is written).

faq.question: What is the relative-correlative pair in Marathi?
faq.answer: जो…तो — जो introduces the relative clause, तो is the correlate in the main clause. Hindi जो…वह becomes जो…तो.

title: Hindi to Marathi Media & News: Politics, Formal Register
description: Media and news vocabulary mapped Hindi to Marathi — political terms, report language, formal register words — from Units 23, 24.
intro: Media and news vocabulary from Units 23–24 mapped Hindi to Marathi — political terms (सरकार→सरकार, मंत्री→मंत्री, चुनाव→निवडणूक), report language (रिपोर्ट→अहवाल, जांच→तपास, घोषणा→घोषणा), formal register (इस प्रकार→या प्रकारे, इसलिए→म्हणून). Each row maps the Hindi formal word to the Marathi equivalent with the register note.
Much political vocabulary is shared Sanskrit loans (सरकार, मंत्री, संसद, विधानसभा) — the shifts are in the functional words and the register conventions (Marathi prefers या प्रकारे over इस प्रकार).
tip: Formal Marathi prefers या प्रकारे (in this manner) over इस प्रकार, म्हणून (therefore) over इसलिए — the logic is the same, the vocabulary is Marathi.

sections.heading: Shared Sanskrit loans — free vocabulary
paragraphs: सरकार, मंत्री, मुख्यमंत्री, प्रधानमंत्री, संसद, विधानसभा, चुनाव→निवडणूक, मतदार, मतदान — the political core is shared. Learn the few that shift: चुनाव→निवडणूक, मत→मत (same), पार्टी→पक्ष.

sections.heading: Register shifts — the functional words
paragraphs: इस प्रकार → या प्रकारे, इसलिए → म्हणून, अतः → त्यामुळे, किन्तु → पण/परंतु, यदि → जर. The logic is identical; the vocabulary is Marathi.

mistakes.why: चुनाव is understood but निवडणूक is the standard Marathi word in news and official use.

mistakes.wrong: Writing इस प्रकार in formal Marathi
mistakes.why: Marathi formal register prefers या प्रकारे; इस प्रकार marks the text as Hindi-influenced.
म्हणून is the standard formal connector; इसलिए is Hindi.

mcq.question: Election in formal Marathi?
mcq.explanation: निवडणूक — the standard Marathi word for election.

mcq.question: “Therefore” in formal Marathi?
mcq.explanation: म्हणून — the standard formal connector.

mcq.question: Party (political) in Marathi?
mcq.explanation: पक्ष (pakṣa) — the standard term; पार्टी is understood.

translate.note: Ergative government + घोषणा केली (feminine agreement with घोषणा).

faq.question: How different is news Marathi from Hindi?
faq.answer: Core political vocabulary is shared Sanskrit loans; functional words shift (इस प्रकार→या प्रकारे, इसलिए→म्हणून, यदि→जर). The grammar (ergative in past, gender agreement) is the same logic.

faq.question: What is “election” in Marathi?
faq.answer: निवडणूक — the standard word in news, official documents and conversation.

title: Hindi to Marathi Business: Trade, Finance
description: Business and finance vocabulary mapped Hindi to Marathi — trade, banking, contracts, formal letters — from Units 19, 23.
intro: Business and finance vocabulary from Units 19, 23 mapped Hindi to Marathi — trade (व्यापार→व्यापार, सौदा→सौदा, ऑर्डर→ऑर्डर), banking (बैंक→बँक, खाता→खाते, ब्याज→व्याज, कर्ज→कर्ज), contracts (अनुबंध→करार, शर्त→शर्त, हस्ताक्षर→स्वाक्षरी). Each row maps the Hindi term to the Marathi equivalent with the register note.

Most finance vocabulary is shared Sanskrit/English loans — the shifts are in the functional words (बैंक→बँक with ँ, चेक→चेक same, रसीद→पावती). Formal letters use the ergative (सरकाराने, कंपनीने) and standard closings (आपला, शुभेच्छा).
tip: पावती = receipt (Marathi); रसीद is Hindi. बँक with ँ (candrabindu) is the Marathi spelling convention for bank.

sections.heading: Banking — mostly shared, spelling shifts
paragraphs: बँक (bank), खाते (account), व्याज (interest), कर्ज (loan), किश्त (installment), चेक (cheque), डिमॅन्ड ड्राफ्ट (demand draft). The candrabindu in बँक is the only spelling flag; the words are shared.

sections.heading: Contracts — native terms where it matters
paragraphs: करार (agreement), शर्त (condition), स्वाक्षरी (signature), गवाह (witness), नोंदणी (registration). These are the words on stamp paper and in legal Marathi — learn them if you sign contracts in Maharashtra.

mistakes.why: Marathi spelling convention for English loans: candrabindu marks the nasal.
रसीद is Hindi; पावती is the Marathi word on every bill and invoice.
हस्ताक्षर is Sanskrit/Hindi formal; स्वाक्षरी is the Marathi legal word.

mcq.question: Receipt in Marathi?
mcq.explanation: पावती (pāvatī) — the word on every Marathi receipt.

mcq.question: Signature in legal Marathi?
mcq.explanation: स्वाक्षरी (svākṣarī) — the legal term; हस्ताक्षर is Sanskrit/Hindi.

mcq.question: Interest in Marathi?
mcq.explanation: व्याज (vyāj) — nasalized from ब्याज.

fill.sentence: कंपनीने करार ___ केला. (The company signed the agreement.)
fill.hint: Ergative company + signature — formal business sentence.

faq.question: What is the Marathi word for “receipt”?
faq.answer: पावती — not रसीद. Every Marathi bill says पावती.

faq.question: How do you write “bank” in Marathi?
faq.answer: बँक — with candrabindu (ँ) over the ब. This is the standard Marathi spelling for the English loan.

title: Hindi to Marathi Advanced Conversation: Idioms, Politeness
description: Advanced conversation patterns mapped Hindi to Marathi — idioms, politeness levels, social nuance, cultural phrases — from Units 25, 26.
intro: Advanced conversation from Units 25–26 mapped Hindi to Marathi — idioms (आमची भेट झाली→आमचं भेट झालं, कृपया→कृपया/हो कृपया), politeness layers (तू/तुम्ही/आप), cultural phrases (राम राम, देवाची कृपा, शुभ प्रवास, काळजी घे), social nuance (काही हरकत नाही, बरोबर, चूक). Each row shows the Hindi social phrase, the Marathi equivalent, and the nuance note.

Marathi politeness is more granular: तू (intimate), तुम्ही (respectful plural/older), आप (formal rare). The rescue lines (मला समजलं नाही, पुन्हा सांगा, हळू बोला) are social lubricant — use them liberally.
tip: When in doubt, use तुम्ही — it is never wrong for elders, strangers, or groups. तू is intimate only.

sections.heading: Politeness ladder
paragraphs: तू (intimate/children) → तुम्ही (respectful plural/older) → आप (formal/official, rare in speech). Hindi आप covers both तुम्ही and आप; Marathi splits them. Default to तुम्ही for anyone older or unfamiliar.

sections.heading: Cultural phrases that carry weight
paragraphs: राम राम (traditional greeting, rural/older), देवाची कृपा (by God's grace — common response to कैसे आहात), शुभ प्रवास (safe journey), काळजी घे (take care), शाबास (well done). These are not decorative — they are social currency.

mistakes.right: तुम्ही — always respectful with service people
mistakes.why: तू with a stranger is rude in Marathi culture. Hindi speakers often default to तू because Hindi आप covers both.

mistakes.right: कृपया or हो कृपया — expected in every request
mistakes.why: Marathi requests without कृपया sound like commands. हो कृपया (yes please) and नको कृपया (no please) are the polite pair.

mistakes.wrong: Assuming राम राम is religious only
mistakes.why: Used by all communities in rural Maharashtra as a neutral hello. Not a religious statement.

mcq.question: Respectful “you” in Marathi?
mcq.explanation: तुम्ही — respectful you for elders, strangers, groups.

mcq.question: “Take care” in Marathi?
mcq.explanation: काळजी घे — literal: care take. The standard caring farewell.

mcq.question: Traditional rural greeting?
mcq.explanation: राम राम — secular cultural greeting across Maharashtra.

faq.question: How many politeness levels does Marathi have for “you”?
faq.answer: Three — तू (intimate), तुम्ही (respectful/standard), आप (formal/rare). Hindi आप covers तुम्ही and आप both.

faq.question: What does काळजी घे mean?
faq.answer: Take care — literal: care take. The standard caring farewell in Marathi, used like ख्याल रखना.
